title: Recover lightweight terminal command evidence
userIntent: Keep a completed ordinary local command readable after in-memory lightweight process state is lost, without replaying the command or creating durable execution ownership for the running command.

intendedBehavior: A completed lightweight command remains readable from bounded terminal evidence after in-memory handle loss.
A missing running handle is never reconstructed by replaying its command.
behavioralInvariants: Running lightweight commands retain no durable lifecycle or lease ownership.
Only bounded terminal evidence may survive memory loss.
Handle recovery never re-executes a command.
regressionRisks: Adding a second process authority or a replay path.
Losing terminal logs and exit evidence after a Runtime-memory reset.
Broadening the change into unrelated Runtime activation or recovery behavior.

provenance.note: The snapshot predates Forge's terminal lightweight-process receipt fix. It is a seed for a future user-facing execution adapter, not a claim that the built-in CLI command solves the task.
